to receive something.

Claude's conclusion:
Host load is healthy (3% CPU, no overcommit), ruling out infra contention as the direct cause.

### Root cause

vaultmgr behaved correctly: the device logs show it fired `"Processing empty EncryptedVaultKeyFromController Application Data Store"` at `2026-11-26T23:42:10.079700853Z` — well within the test's 5-minute wait window (since `23:39:48Z`). The test failure is not a vaultmgr logic bug; it's that this log record never reached the controller. Live on-device evidence pins this precisely: `/run/loguploader/NewlogMetrics/global.json` shows `FailedToSend:true` with `FailSentStartTime: 2026-11-26T23:41:48Z` and no successful upload since, while `logread` shows Vector's `parse_json_upload` transform continuously emitting `vector_buffers::buffer_usage_data: Buffer counter overflowed. Clamping value to u64::MAX` every ~10s from 23:41:48 straight through to the current time (23:47:47+) — the newlog delivery pipeline to the controller is stalled, not vaultmgr's logic.

This is the identical Vector buffer-overflow bug already recorded in `live-ledger.md`'s run #61 entry (same suite, same test `TestVaultWithoutControllerKeyOnExt4`, same `FailedToSend`/buffer-overflow signature, just a different assertion checkpoint within the test timed out) and in run #56 against the sibling test `TestVaultKeyModeRecoveryOnExt4`. So this is a known, recurring issue as of today (2026-11-26), not new — any vault test depending on a controller-delivered log record is vulnerable to it, and it has now reproduced for a third time tonight across two different tests in this suite.

Claude's conclusion:
### Root cause

After the test's second controller-signing-cert rotation and its `device.SoftReboot(true)` at 14:13:24, zedagent never recovers connectivity with the controller. From 14:14 onward it repeatedly fetches `/certs` successfully but then fails AuthContainer verification against *both* `controllercerts` and `controllercerts.bak` (`SenderStatusCertMiss … local server cert hash does not match in authen`), flip-flopping between two cert-set hashes on successive fetches rather than converging. Because verification never succeeds, the device can't complete TPM attestation (`attestation_info` is stuck in `ATTESTATION_STATE_NONCE_WAIT`), so it never obtains a fresh `IntegrityToken` after reboot — and Adam's log shows every subsequent `/config` poll rejected with "integrity token missmatch" continuously from 14:14 through the end of the capture (14:25+), vs. only a brief, self-resolving mismatch blip around 13:50-13:51 during the earlier (pre-reboot) rotation. With config fetch permanently stuck, zedmanager has no `AppInstanceConfig` for either app post-reboot and only app1's pre-existing `AppInstanceStatus`/domain survived; `signing-cert-app2`'s domain was never recreated (no DomainStatus, no listed `appInstances` entry), so the port-forward to 172.20.20.123:2223 has nothing behind it — exactly the SSH timeout reported.

This matches the exact risk the test's own doc comment calls out for the second rotation ("the installed certificate no longer matches controllercerts.bak … a stale cached serverSigningCertHash shows up here"), now manifesting as a permanent deadlock once compounded with a reboot, rather than resolving at the `signing-cert-rotated-2` checkpoint as intended. This failure/signature (`TestControllerSigningCertChange`, SenderStatusCertMiss / integrity-token deadlock) does not appear anywhere in the prior nightly ledger, so this is a new occurrence, not a known recurring issue, and it is unrelated to any other failure earlier in this run (the adjacent VTPM suite failures are a different area).

Claude's conclusion:
### Root cause

vaultmgr behaved exactly as the test expects: after phase 2's reboot (PCR14 changed, controller's escrowed key cleared), I confirmed directly on the live device (`logread`) that it logged `"Vault cleanup is not allowed"` at 15:11:16.893, since `vault.IsVaultCleanupAllowed()` correctly returned false (no cleanup sentinel present). The test failed only because that record never reached the controller within the 5-minute `waitForVaultmgrLog` window — Adam's last received log batch for this device ends at 15:09:56.744 (pre-reboot shutdown messages), nothing since, even 10+ minutes after the post-reboot boot at 15:10:16. Live `logread -f` on the device shows Vector's `parse_json_keep` **and** `parse_json_upload` transforms both continuously emitting `vector_buffers::buffer_usage_data: Buffer counter overflowed. Clamping value to u64::MAX` every ~250ms since boot, and `/run/loguploader/NewlogMetrics/global.json` shows `"FailedToSend":true` with `FailSentStartTime: 2026-11-26T15:11:07Z` and no successful upload since — i.e. the newlog pipeline that ships `vaultmgr` records to the controller is stalled, not vaultmgr's logic. (Separately, `evetest eve logs`/non-follow log fetch appears to be a harness-side artifact returning stale pre-reboot output — live `ssh`+`logread` shows the device is fully up and otherwise healthy, including working controller connectivity.)

This is a recurrence of the same Vector buffer-overflow bug already recorded today earlier in this same ledger, under run #56, for the sibling test `TestVaultKeyModeRecoveryOnExt4` in this same suite (same `parse_json_keep`/`buffer_usage_data` signature, same effect of stalling newlog delivery to the controller) — so this is a known, recurring issue as of today (2026-11-26), not a new one, now reproducing in a different test because any vault test that depends on a controller-delivered log record is vulnerable to it. It is unrelated to the other failure already investigated in this run (`TestControllerSigningCertChange`'s cert-verification/attestation deadlock) — different mechanism entirely. The broker host is currently overcommitted (102% of host RAM assigned to running VMs, swap in use), which plausibly aggravates Vector's CPU/buffer contention, though the earlier same-bug occurrence today happened under modest host load, suggesting this is an underlying Vector/newlog defect rather than purely an infra-overload artifact.

Timed out after 120.001s.

Claude's conclusion:
### Root cause

`vaultmgr` behaved correctly: the device-side agent log confirms the fault landed and was handled exactly as designed — `"Vault config inited with tpmkeyonly false"` was logged at `23:35:49.124`, followed immediately by the correct retry/success sequence (`23:35:50.100`–`23:35:50.473`, `tpmKeyOnly=false` failing, `tpmKeyOnly=true` opening the vault, and the corrected mode being persisted). The test failed not because that message is missing, but because it never reaches the on-device location the test's `newlogCount()` helper polls (`/persist/newlog/collect/dev.log.keep.*` + `/persist/newlog/keepSentQueue/*.gz`), which by design is read instead of the controller because controller delivery is "too late" for this test's window.

Live evidence shows why: the `vector` process (pid 2577) has been pegged at ~77% CPU since this exact boot, continuously emitting `transform{...component_id=parse_json_keep...}: vector_buffers::buffer_usage_data: Buffer counter overflowed. Clamping value to u64::MAX` every ~10s, non-stop, from `23:35:xx` through the present (`23:42+`). This is the Vector transform feeding the "keep" sink (`dev_keep_sink` → `/run/devKeep_sink.sock`, a 256MB disk buffer with `when_full: block`). Correspondingly, `/persist/newlog/collect/dev.log.keep.*` (the device's local "keep" log file, containing only the boot-time `devID`/`eveVersion` header, 111 bytes) and `/persist/newlog/keepSentQueue/` have not received a single new record since `23:35:31` — frozen at the exact moment this Vector pipeline stalled — while the parallel "upload" pipeline (`parse_json_upload` → `devUpload`) kept rotating and shipping chunks to the controller normally the whole time (confirming network/controller connectivity and `loguploader` were fine, and explaining why `evetest eve logs`, which reflects what reached the controller, does show the message).

This does not match the previously-logged `TestVaultKeyModeRecoveryOnExt4` ledger entries (stale attempt-count assertion, reboot-timeout-under-host-load, or the earlier newlogd-rotation race) — none of those involve Vector or a stuck "keep" buffer, and a search of `live-ledger.md` for `parse_json_keep`/`vector_buffers`/"Buffer counter overflowed" returns no prior hits, so this looks like a new, not-previously-recorded failure mode. Host load on the broker is modest (6% CPU, no swap pressure beyond baseline), ruling out infra overload as the trigger. No shared root cause with any other failure exists in this run (it's the only failure so far). No PR diff was supplied for this investigation.

Claude's conclusion:
### Root cause

This is a different, more specific failure mode than any prior `TestVaultKeyModeRecoveryOnExt4` entry. Live `vaultmgr` logs show that after the test recorded the wrong `TpmKeyOnly` mode and rebooted (22:54:53), the device's first unlock attempt logged `"can't read the legacy disk key, generating a new one"` — a message that only comes from `evetpm.FetchVaultKey` (the *un-sealed*, TPM-NVRAM "legacy key" path), never from the sealed-key path (`FetchSealedVaultKey`, which instead logs `"sealed disk key present int TPM, about to unseal it"` — exactly what the *prior*, successful boot at 22:52:58 had logged). The live `VaultStatus` on the device right now confirms this: `"PCRStatus":2` (`PCR_DISABLED`), versus `PCR_ENABLED` on the healthy prior boot. Per `pkg/pillar/evetpm/tpm.go`, `FetchSealedVaultKey` falls back to the legacy/non-sealed `FetchVaultKey` whenever `PCRBankSHA256Enabled()` — a live, cached-once-per-process `ReadPCR(0, SHA256)` probe against the TPM — returns false. Since no legacy TPM-NVRAM key existed yet (this vault was always sealed-key-based), that first attempt minted a brand-new random key and wrote it into TPM NVRAM, which obviously can't open the real fscrypt-protected vault (`Error unlocking vault: exit status 1`), and the fallback retry just re-reads that same freshly-written garbage key again. Critically, the controller-key rescue path (`vaultmgr.go:594-611`, `Re-sealing disk key` → `UnlockDefaultVault`) re-seals the correct key into TPM but then calls `unlockVault(..., useSealedKey=true)` again, which hits the exact same disabled-PCR-bank branch and ignores the freshly re-sealed key in favor of the unrelated legacy NVRAM key — so even the controller rescue can't recover, leaving the vault permanently in `DATASEC_AT_REST_ERROR` (status 4) for the rest of the boot, matching the test's failure exactly.

This does not match either of the two previously-recorded `TestVaultKeyModeRecoveryOnExt4` failure signatures in `live-ledger.md` (a slow-VM reboot-timeout, last seen 2026-11-04/05, and a stale hardcoded attempt-count assertion recurring 2026-10-29 through 11-02) — both of those hit different line numbers (`vault_keymode_test.go:298`/`:318`) and different mechanisms. Tonight's failure (line 343, vault genuinely stuck in error after the controller key) is new, not previously recorded. There's no other failure in this run's artifacts so far to share a root cause with, and I found no evidence this is simply infra/host-load flakiness — it's a reproducible code path confirmed by matching log strings to their exact source locations.

### Root cause

Live `domainmgr` logs show the exact same signature already diagnosed twice before in this ledger: at `23:09:00.446` the app's vTPM launch request to `vtpmd` hit `context deadline exceeded` (domainmgr's fixed `swtpmTimeout` client timeout, `pkg/pillar/hypervisor/kvm.go:2311-2320`), so domainmgr set `status.VirtualTPM = false` and continued on to build/boot the qemu domain **without any TPM device** (`pkg/pillar/cmd/domainmgr/domainmgr.go:1426-1429`/`2052-2055` show this path explicitly falls through rather than retrying or failing activation). Crucially, `vtpmd` itself succeeded just ~2s later — `"vTPM launched SWTPM instance with id: b4810ae9-..., pid: 58"` at `23:09:02.000` — but by then domainmgr had already moved on (domain created at `23:09:06`, RUNNING by `23:09:12`), so the guest came up with no `/dev/tpm0`/`/dev/tpmrm0` and no swtpm socket, exactly matching the test's TCTI "no such file"/connection-refused errors.

This is a known, recurring issue per `live-ledger.md`: the identical "domainmgr's fixed swtpm-launch timeout races vtpmd's slower-but-successful launch, producing a TPM-less guest" mechanism was first diagnosed on **2026-11-02** (`TestAppVTPMIdentitySurvivesReboots`, where a ~58s PCR-unseal blocked the handler against a 10s timeout) and recurred on **2026-11-05** (`TestAppVTPMBackupRecoversPrimaryCorruption`). Tonight's occurrence is the same unfixed domainmgr/vtpmd timeout race hitting a third test (`TestAppVTPMProtectedFailurePreservesState`), not a new regression — only the specific trigger for the slow/delayed `vtpmd` response differs (here likely contention from the test's preceding deliberate "protected failure" cycle at `23:06:54`, which logged a 424 "PCR-protected SWTPM state could not be loaded; state preserved" response just ~2 minutes earlier). No other failures were recorded in this run's artifacts to compare against for a shared root cause.

The test's `expectGuestTPMMarker` timed out because the guest VM for app `vtpm-backup` (`54a464b1-...`) was launched with **no vTPM device at all**: the live `/run/domainmgr/domains/dom1.cfg` for that domain has zero `tpm`/`tpmdev` entries, so `/dev/tpm0`/`/dev/tpmrm0` never appear in the guest, matching the exact `tcti` "no such file" errors in the failure. It did not recur on 2026-11-03 or 2026-11-04 per the ledger, so this is a known/recurring issue first seen 2026-11-02, reappearing tonight (2026-11-05) on a different test exercising the same vtpmd/domainmgr timeout race, not a new regression. Per the ledger, this specific reboot-timeout failure mode first appeared 2026-11-04 and is now recurring a second night in a row, so it's a known/recurring infrastructure-contention issue, not a new regression.
